sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Ms Deepshikha, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel appearing for the State.

2. This is 3rd petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking a direction for giving compassionate appointment under The U.P. Recruitment of Dependants of Government Servants Dying in Harness Rules, 1974 to the petitioner.

entities.text: U.P. Recruitment of Dependants of Government Servants Dying in Harness Rules, 1974
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. First petition was filed by the petitioner in the year 2012, being Writ Petition No.7616(SS) of 2012 after the death of his father on 15.01.2011 in harness, who was employed as Constable in Civil Police.

entities.text: Vinod Pandey vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court disposed of the said writ petition vide order dated 21.12.2012 with a direction to Superintendent of Police, Balrampur to consider and decide the claim of the petitioner with regard to the compassionate appointment, in case the petitioner was found eligible, the competent authority would consider the appointment of the petitioner.

5. In compliance of the said order, Superintendent of Police, Balrampur vide order dated 22.02.2013 decided the claim of the petitioner and held that the petitioner was facing criminal trial of Sessions Trial No.11 of 2015 arising out of Case Crime No.145 of 2011, under Sections 498A, 302, 201 IPC,
Police Station Sirsia, District Shrawasti, therefore, till the pendency of the trial of criminal case against the petitioner, he would not be offered appointment on compassionate ground, however, it was said that any other dependant can move an application, whose character was good but no such application was moved by the other dependant.
6.

It appears that the petitioner got acquitted in Sessions Trial No.11 of 2015 (supra) and, thereafter he filed second petition being Writ Petition No.6267(SS) of 2013, and the said writ petition was disposed of vide order dated 14.10.2020 with a direction to the Superintendent of Police, Balrampur to take appropriate decision on the representation of the petitioner dated 19.12.2019 preferred by the petitioner.
7. In pursuance to the aforesaid order, representation of the petitioner has not been decided.
There is already a direction for deciding the representation of the petitioner, therefore, for the same cause of action, successive writ petitions would not be maintainable.
Therefore, the writ petition is dismissed leaving it open to the petitioner to resort any other remedy, as may be available to him under law.
